insights.summary: Priya, your balance is likely to dip below £0 around 1 December when rent goes out, but staying within your £1,500 overdraft until your Student Finance payment on 12 Jan looks very likely, and small changes can shorten the time you spend overdrawn.

alerts.title: Rent may take you into your overdraft
alerts.message: Your £520 Unite Students rent on 1 December is likely to take your balance below £0, to around -£134. It's very likely you'll stay overdrawn until your Student Finance England payment of £1,650 on 12 January.
alerts.why: Our forecast shows a 99% chance of going below £0 within 30 days, with a median date of 1 December, and only a 1% chance of going past your overdraft limit in the next 90 days.
alerts.action: Check whether your overdraft is interest-free as a student, so you know what being overdrawn until 12 January will cost.

alerts.title: Your safe-to-spend until 12 January
alerts.message: To stay within your £1,500 overdraft until 12 January, try to keep everyday spending under £21 a day. You usually spend about £16 a day, so you have some room, but December spending last year was about £484 higher than a typical month.
alerts.why: Safe-to-spend within your overdraft is £21.21 a day over the 65 days to your next Student Finance payment, compared with your typical £15.98 a day. Last December you spent £387 to £580 more than usual.
alerts.action: Try a 48-hour wait before any non-essential buy over £30, especially in December.

alerts.title: Two changes that cut your days overdrawn
alerts.message: Spending half as much on going out (about £65 a month) could cut your expected days overdrawn from about 61 to 50. Halving shopping as well (about £40 a month) could bring it down to about 43 days and lift your lowest expected balance from -£1,006 to -£794.
alerts.why: Our action plan tested these changes over the next 120 days across simulated futures. We also noticed that in the 3 days after money comes in, non-essential spending is about 8.3 times your usual.
alerts.action: When your loan arrives on 12 January, move your going-out and shopping money into a separate pot so your main account just covers bills.

alerts.title: Turn your loan into a weekly allowance
alerts.message: Your income comes in large lumps, which can make it hard to pace spending. Moving each loan payment into your £150 Easy Saver and paying yourself a set amount each week could help it last and start your savings goal.
alerts.why: Your income arrives a few times a year, your savings haven't grown in 6 months, and they would cover about 0.6 months of spending against a target of £3,120.
alerts.action: On 12 January, move the £1,650 to your Easy Saver and set up a weekly transfer back, dividing it by the weeks until your next payment.
